## What does this PR do?

When a column is hidden from the Table header's context menu, the focused header cell is unmounted and focus falls to `<body>` — the next Tab press restarts keyboard navigation from the top of the page instead of staying in the table.

This PR keeps focus in the table by computing which visible column takes the hidden one's position and calling the grid's `setActivePosition` to focus that column's header after the re-render.

Fixes #135901

## Requirements

Before submitting this PR, please make sure:

- [x] You have read the [contributing guide](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] You have included tests for the changes (if applicable)
- [x] You have tested the changes or added tests for the changes (if applicable)

## Notes to the reviewer

This can be verified manually on the "Panel Tests - Table - Kitchen Sink" dashboard with `table.refresh` and `table.refreshNewFeatures` feature toggles enabled:

1. Tab into a column header
2. Open the column menu with Enter
3. Navigate to "Hide column" and press Enter
4. Focus should stay on the next column's header (not `<body>`)

The e2e test referenced in the issue (`table-keyboard-a11y.spec.ts`) is part of the separate a11y test suite; this change should make that test pass.

issue.title: fix(image-uploader): use functional update in async delete to avoid stale closure
issue.body:
## Why

`ImageUploader`'s `onDelete` handler awaits an async confirmation (e.g. `Dialog.confirm`) before removing the item. While that promise is pending, an upload can complete and call `setValue(prev => prev.concat(newVal))`. The old code then executed:

```tsx
setValue(value.filter((x, i) => i !== index))
```

using the `value` array and `index` captured at render time — the stale closure discards the concurrent upload, or removes the wrong item when overlapping deletes shift the indices.

## What changed

Switch to a functional update and filter by item reference instead of index:

```tsx
setValue(prev => prev.filter(x => x !== fileItem))
```

This reads the latest state at resolution time and is immune to index shifts from concurrent mutations.

Fixes #7087

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Checklist

- [x] I have run `npx tsc --noEmit` and there are no TypeScript errors
- [x] I have run `npm run lint` and there are no linting errors
- [x] I have run `npm test` and all tests pass with my changes

## How has this been tested

- Added a regression test that reproduces the race: two initial items, click delete on the first (async promise stays pending), upload a new file while pending, then resolve the deletion. The test asserts the new upload survives — it would be silently discarded with the old stale-closure filter.
- The fix changes one line in the `onDelete` handler; the rest of the component is untouched.

**`setActivePosition` alone never moves DOM focus.** Reading `@grafana/react-data-grid@7.0.0-beta.60` (the pinned version): the imperative handle only updates the roving-tabindex selection; the grid only calls `focus()` when the position is set with `{ shouldFocus: true }` (`setPositionToFocus` → `focusCell`). issue.body:
Fixes #7962

## Why

A stale `memory.backend_config` (DeerMem-only keys left in place after
switching `manager_class` to `openviking`) surfaced only when
`MemoryMiddleware` constructed `OpenVikingMemoryManager`
mid-conversation — after the model run had already consumed tokens.
`make doctor` reported Ready because `MemoryConfig` accepts
`backend_config` as untyped data, so the mismatch was invisible until a
chat turn failed.

## What changed

`make doctor` now statically validates the selected memory backend's
`backend_config`. For `openviking` (or a dotted path to
`OpenVikingMemoryManager`) it runs the backend's own side-effect-free
validator, `OpenVikingConfig.from_backend_config`, and reports the
offending keys exactly as the runtime error would (e.g. "Unknown
OpenViking backend_config fields: debounce_seconds, ...").

- Backends without a static validator (`deermem`, `mem0`, `noop`) are
  skipped rather than half-checked; extending the pattern to them only
  needs a validator call.
- Memory disabled → skip; config that fails to load is already reported
  by the existing loadable check, so this check does not double-report.

## Surface area

- [x] **Backend API** — no; this is the `scripts/doctor.py` diagnostic
  path only (no runtime behavior change, no endpoint change)

## Bug fix verification

- Test path: `backend/tests/test_doctor_script.py`
  (`TestMemoryBackendConfigCheck`, five cases: stale field fails and
  names the key; valid config passes; other backends skipped; disabled
  memory skipped; dotted manager path validated)
- Red on main, green on this branch: **yes** — the fail/skip assertions
  exercise `check_memory_backend_config`, which does not exist on main.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/test_doctor_script.py`: 9 passed (4 existing + 5 new)
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both files
- End-to-end with a synthetic `config.yaml` (`manager_class: openviking`
  plus the example's DeerMem `backend_config`): doctor now fails with
  the full unknown-fields list; with only OpenViking keys and an API key
  env set, it reports ok. Both runs use `DEER_FLOW_CONFIG_PATH` and the
  backend `PYTHONPATH`, mirroring `make doctor`.

## AI assistance

**Tool(s) used:** ZCode (AI coding agent)

**How you used it:** read the config/validation code paths, drafted the
check and tests, and ran the doctor end-to-end locally; a human
reviewed every line and takes responsibility for the change.

- [x] I've read and understand every line of this change and take
  responsibility for it — it's not unreviewed AI output.

issue.title: Markdown writers: separate adjacent inline elements
issue.body:
Closes #11993. Split out of #12006 at jgm's request (one PR per issue).

Adjacent inline elements that run together in the output read back
differently than they were written: back-to-back code spans join into
one span (`#11993`), and emphasis-like elements whose delimiter runs
touch fuse or vanish (e.g. `[Emph, Emph]` → `*hi**hi*` reads back as
literal text; `[Strong, Strong]` fuses into one element).

`inlineListToMarkdown` now inserts a zero-width space between adjacent
elements that would run together, in one pass before rendering:

- Code spans, unless an attribute block is written after the first
  (which already separates them);
- Emph, Strong, and — where the variant enables them — Strikeout,
  Subscript and Superscript;
- nothing is inserted in the plain text variant, which has no
  delimiters.

Pairs that do not run together (e.g. `Emph` next to `Strong`, `Emph`
next to `Strikeout`) get no separator; these were checked by
round-tripping every adjacent pair through the 3.13 release binary.

Tests: `test/command/11993-adjacent-code.md` covers code spans with
and without attributes, gfm, the emphasis-like elements, and a reader
check that the zero-width space reads back as a separate `Str`.

issue.body:
Fixes #7858

## Why

Issue #7858: `extract_skills()` built one flat `tool_call_id -> path`
map over the whole conversation. Tool-call ids are unique per response,
not per conversation, so a later read that reused an id overwrote the
earlier read's path: the earlier skill silently dropped out of the
`## Active skills` ledger, and its correct ToolMessage logged a
spurious "mismatched skill read metadata" warning.

## What changed

`extract_skills` now rebuilds the map from each AIMessage's own calls
and resolves a ToolMessage against the nearest preceding response —
the pairing rule `tool_call_args.pair_tool_call_results` already
applies. `loaded_at` keeps its ToolMessage index.

Note on approach: a prior PR for this issue (#7860) was withdrawn by
its author, and Copilot review there flagged queue-consumption

issue.title: Markdown writers: escape thematic break and setext lookalikes
issue.body:
Closes #11992, closes #11993, closes #11994.

Three separate round-trip bugs in the Markdown writers. They touch
overlapping code (`Markdown/Inline.hs`, `Markdown.hs`), so they are in one
PR; I can split them if you prefer.

**#11992 — lines that read back as thematic breaks or setext headings.**
A paragraph, or a line after a `LineBreak`, consisting only of dashes or
equals was written unescaped and read back as a thematic break or setext
heading underline. `escapeLineStart` now escapes the first character of
such a run, but only when `escapeText` leaves the run untouched, so
`markdown` with `smart` keeps its existing `\-\--` and gains nothing new.
The wrapping case is handled separately: `avoidBadWraps` keeps a final run
of dashes or equals on the previous line instead of adding a backslash to
ordinary text, which is what #3542 was worried about.

**#11993 — adjacent `Code` inlines.**
Two adjacent code spans were written back to back, so the closing backtick
of the first and the opening backtick of the second formed a run of two
inside one span; the result read back as a single `Code` containing
backticks. Markdown cannot express two adjacent code spans, so adjacent
`Code` inlines are now merged into one span with the combined text — but
only when nothing would be written between them. When the first span has
attributes that the writer emits, the spans are already separated by the
`{...}` and no merge happens.

**#11994 — link titles and character references in destinations.**
Titles were written between double quotes without escaping `"` or `\`,
which made gfm and commonmark readers fail to recognize the link at all;
images and reference-link definitions used the same code. Destinations
were written as is, so `¶` in a URL was decoded to `¶` on read back.
Titles are now escaped, and `&` is escaped when it begins a character
reference, mirroring what `escapeText` already does for text.

`test/writer.markdown` gains the escaped titles on three lines; all three
tests are in `test/command`.

issue.title: HTML writer: give footnote back-links an accessible name
issue.body:
Closes #11965.

The web-page footnote back-link carried only the arrow U+21A9 (+U+FE0E),
which screen readers announce as "leftwards arrow with hook, variation
selector 15" — no indication that it returns to the reference. The
`doc-backlink` role does not supply a name on macOS (per DPUB-AAM it
exposes as a plain link).

## Change

HTML5 back-links now carry
`aria-label="Back to reference N"` (N = the note number). The visible
markup is otherwise unchanged; the arrow and the variation selector stay
exactly as they were.

The label text is a new `BackToReference` term in `data/translations/`.
`en.yaml` defines it; the writer falls back to the English label
**without emitting a `NoTranslation` warning** when the active language
does not define the term, so documents in other languages are unaffected
even under `--fail-if-warnings`. Other languages can pick the term up
whenever their files are updated; I did not add machine translations.

HTML4 output and the EPUB paths are unchanged (the attribute is gated on
html5, and the EPUB back-link already spells out the note number).

## Test updates

- `test/writer.html5` and the five command tests that carry back-link
  markup (`4235`, `7006`, `8770-block`, `8770-section`,
  `8770-document`) are updated for the new attribute, with line
  wrapping recomputed for the longer tag.
- `test/command/11965.md` is new: it checks the attribute itself, the
  translation fallback under `--fail-if-warnings -M lang=de` (a German
  file without the term must not warn), and that HTML4 output is
  unchanged.

## Verification scope

No GHC on this machine, so I could not run the suite; CI here is the
verification. The expected outputs were derived from the 3.13 release
binary's current output plus the attribute addition, and the wrapping
was recomputed following the layout rule in `Text.DocLayout` (break at
an attribute boundary when `column + 1 + width(next atom) > columns`),
validated by reproducing the *current* goldens with the same rule
before applying the change. If anything still mismatches, I will fix
it here rather than leave it to you.

comment.body:
Second fix on the same spot, sorry for the round trip.

My previous version used a list comprehension with a guard and two
elements:

```haskell
let kvs = [ ("role","doc-backlink")
          , ("aria-label", backlinkText <> " " <> ref)
          | html5 ]
```

which does not parse (`parse error on input '|'` at 1755:17 on all GHC
versions). Replaced with an explicit conditional in bde372b:

```haskell
let kvs = if html5
             then [ ("role","doc-backlink")
                  , ("aria-label", backlinkText <> " " <> ref) ]
             else []
```

from becoming a third round, I re-read the whole binding before pushing

from `gets stHtml5` at the top of `blockListToNote`, and

because `PandocMonad` has a `MonadTrans` instance (the `translateTerm`

The HTML4/EPUB paths are untouched now: both attributes are inside the

issue.title: Cancelled turns keep scheduling timers; the deadline-timer regression test fails on main
issue.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

`AgentTaskService` keeps scheduling timers after a turn is cancelled, and they
are never reclaimed. A cancelled turn leaves the process with a growing number
of pending timers, and the existing regression test for this — `clears task
deadline timers when completion wins the race` in
`packages/agent-core-v2/test/agent/task/taskManager.test.ts` — fails on `main`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On `main` (`c97d13b4`), with the repository's own test environment:

```sh
cd packages/agent-core-v2
pnpm vitest run test/agent/task/taskManager.test.ts
```

The single test passes when run alone:

```sh
pnpm vitest run test/agent/task/taskManager.test.ts -t "clears task deadline timers"
```

but fails when the whole file runs:

```
AssertionError: expected 8 to be less than or equal to 3
 ❯ test/agent/task/taskManager.test.ts:1323:32
```

CI reproduces it too, with a larger number: `expected 41 to be less than or
equal to 3` (run 40846750768, job `test (2)`).

### What is the expected behavior?

After a turn is cancelled, timers created by that turn should be cleared, and
`vi.getTimerCount()` should return to its pre-cancel baseline.

### Actual behaviour, measured

I instrumented the test to sample `vi.getTimerCount()` at each step:

```
baseline=3  afterWait=3  afterCancel=3  afterAdvanceTimersByTime(0)=8
then advancing 1000ms five times:  8 → 16 → 16 → 17 → 19 → 19
```

`loop.cancel()` itself creates nothing, but the microtask flush that follows
schedules eight timers, and the count then grows monotonically instead of
settling. That growth is the part that looks wrong rather than merely
"timers still pending".

I also wrapped `setTimeout` during that flush to record the delays that get
scheduled:

```
[10000, 3000, 3000, 1000, 1000, 1000, 1000, 1000]
```

The repeated `1000` looks like a poll and the `3000`/`10000` like backoff, i.e.
work that keeps rescheduling itself after the turn is already cancelled.

### Where it seems to come from

`packages/agent-core-v2/src/_base/utils/retry.ts`:

```ts
export async function sleepForRetry(delayMs: number, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void> {
  signal?.throwIfAborted();
  const sleepPromise = sleep(delayMs);
  if (signal === undefined) {
    await sleepPromise;
    return;
  }
  await abortable(sleepPromise, signal);
}

function sleep(delayMs: number): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    setTimeout(resolve, delayMs);
  });
}
```

Two problems here:

1. When `signal` is `undefined` the retry sleep cannot be interrupted at all.
2. Even when a `signal` is passed, `abortable` only settles the promise early —
   the underlying `setTimeout` from `sleep()` is never `clearTimeout`ed, so the
   timer stays in the queue until its full delay elapses.

The same shape appears in `taskService.ts` `terminateWithGrace`, where
`graceTimer` is cleared only after `Promise.race` settles; if the other branch
never settles the timer is held for the full grace period.

### Version and environment

- Version: `main` at `c97d13b4`
- Platform: Windows 11, Node v24.15.0, pnpm 12.16.1
- The failure is deterministic locally when the whole file runs, and also
  occurs in CI, so it does not need a live model or a deployed Gateway.

### Why I am filing this rather than sending a PR

I did not attempt a fix. The change has to touch how cancellation propagates
into the retry and poll loops, and I could not convince myself that a small
patch would preserve the existing concurrency guarantees — a wrong fix here is
worse than a reported bug. If a maintainer can point at the intended place to
cancel these chains, I am happy to write the patch and the regression test.

One thing worth deciding either way: if the current assertion is considered too
strict for a fake-timer test, the test could be relaxed instead — but the
monotonic growth above suggests there is real leaked work behind it, not just an
imprecise assertion.

issue.title: fix(mcp): keep a tool argument named runtime out of LangGraph's runtime injection
issue.body:
Fixes #7675

## Why

A valid MCP tool argument named `runtime` was dropped when a tool ran through the pooled stdio wrapper or the durable background-submit wrapper. Both took LangGraph's `ToolRuntime` in a parameter named `runtime`, and `ToolNode` injects the runtime by that name, so it overwrote the model's value. The server then received the other arguments only (a missing-field error when `runtime` is required, a silent default when optional), and `TaskSubmitRequest.arguments` lacked it.

## What changed

The injected runtime parameter in `call_with_persistent_session` and `submit_in_background` is now called `deerflow_runtime` (still detected through its `ToolRuntime` annotation: `_get_all_injected_args(tool).runtime` now reports `deerflow_runtime`, asserted in `test_func_patched_mcp_tool_keeps_toolnode_runtime_injection`), and the personal-MCP ownership guard in `mcp/user_tools.py` looks the injected parameter name up per tool (`deerflow_runtime` for pooled stdio, the adapter's `runtime` for HTTP/SSE), covered for both by `test_personal_tool_guard_reads_the_injected_runtime_for_either_transport`. `mcp/AGENTS.md` describes the new injection rule. Business arguments reach the tool unchanged, including one called `runtime`. Existing tests that call the wrappers directly now pass `deerflow_runtime=`.

## Surface area

- [x] **Agents / LangGraph** — tool wrapper parameter used for runtime injection (no graph, prompt or schema change)

## Bug fix verification

- Test paths: `tests/test_mcp_task_tool_wrapping.py::test_submit_wrapper_keeps_a_business_argument_named_runtime` (submit wrapper, through a real `ToolNode`) and `tests/test_mcp_session_pool.py::test_session_pool_tool_keeps_a_business_argument_named_runtime` (pooled wrapper, same way).
- Red on `main`, green on this branch: yes for both (`{'code': 'print(1)'} != {'runtime': 'python', 'code': 'print(1)'}` on main).

## Validation

- `tests/test_personal_mcp.py`, `tests/test_mcp_task_tool_wrapping.py`, `tests/test_mcp_session_pool.py`: 133 passed after the guard follow-up; before it, `pytest tests -k mcp`: 1782 passed, 39 skipped (the full suite was not run).
- `ruff check` on the touched files: clean; `ruff format --check` on the touched source and the two new-test files: clean.

## AI assistance

**Tool(s) used:** Claude Code.

**How you used it:** Claude Code investigated the injection in `langgraph.prebuilt.tool_node`, made the change and wrote the tests.

- [ ] I've read and understand every line of this change and take responsibility for it — it's not unreviewed AI output. (to be ticked by the human who files it)

comment.body:
I had opened #7676 for the same root cause and closed it in favour of this one —
yours covers `user_tools.py` and the existing call sites, which mine did not.

While investigating I verified the chain that makes the rename safe, in case it
is useful for review (I could not run tests locally, so this is from reading the
installed-source contracts rather than from execution):

1. **Injection is annotation-driven, not name-driven.** LangGraph's
   `ToolNode._get_all_injected_args` resolves injected parameters via
   `get_type_hints` and stores the discovered *names*, so a renamed parameter
   annotated `Runtime` is still injected.

2. **The remote `args_schema` does not strip the extra key.**
   `langchain-mcp-adapters` sets `args_schema` to the MCP `inputSchema`, which is
   a JSON-schema **dict**, not a Pydantic model. In `langchain_core.tools.base`,
   `_parse_input` returns dict input unchanged and `_to_args_and_kwargs` turns
   every key into a keyword argument. (For a Pydantic schema the extra injected
   key *would* be filtered out — worth keeping in mind if the adapter ever
   switches to a model schema.)

3. **`StructuredTool._arun` forwards kwargs directly to the coroutine**, so the
   renamed parameter and `**arguments` are both bound correctly.

One thing to double-check when you can run the suite: `test_mcp_session_pool.py`
has calls like `coroutine(runtime=None, x=1)` that rely on the `get_config()`
fallback. After the rename those need to pass `deerflow_runtime=None` instead,

issue.title: MCP: keep a business argument named `runtime` in tool wrappers
issue.body:
Closes #7675.

Both DeerFlow-owned MCP wrappers declared the framework `ToolRuntime` as a
parameter literally named `runtime`:

- `_make_session_pool_tool` → `call_with_persistent_session`
- `_make_background_submit_tool` → `submit_in_background`

The wrapped tool keeps the remote `args_schema`, so a server may legitimately
declare a business property with that name. LangGraph then injects the runtime
into the same key, Python binds it to the explicit parameter, and only
`**arguments` is forwarded — the business value is gone before the remote
schema ever sees it.

## Fix

Rename the framework parameter in both wrappers. Injection is driven by the
`Runtime` annotation, not by the name, so nothing else changes. The renamed
parameter is added to the call by the framework and forwarded to the coroutine,
while the business `runtime` key stays in `**arguments` untouched.

Why this is safe with the remote schema: `langchain-mcp-adapters` sets
`args_schema` to the MCP `inputSchema`, which is a JSON-schema **dict**, not a
Pydantic model. `BaseTool._parse_input` returns dict input unchanged, and
`_to_args_and_kwargs` turns every key into a keyword argument, so the extra
injected key reaches the coroutine signature.

## Test

`backend/tests/test_mcp_tool_runtime_argument.py` calls the pooled wrapper
directly with a runtime object and a business `runtime` value, and asserts the
remote call receives `{"runtime": "python", "code": "print(1)"}`. Calling the
wrapper directly mirrors the post-injection call and avoids needing a real
stdio server.

## Verification scope — please read

I could not run this test locally. This machine has no `langgraph`,
`langchain-mcp-adapters` or `uv`, and package installation and `git clone`
both fail here with connection resets, so I could not execute the regression
or the repository suite. **The test above has not been run.**

What I did verify, by reading the installed-source contracts:

- LangGraph injects `ToolRuntime` by type annotation, with the parameter name
  discovered dynamically (`_get_all_injected_args` via `get_type_hints`), so a
  renamed parameter is still injected.
- `langchain-mcp-adapters` uses the MCP `inputSchema` as `args_schema`
  (a JSON-schema dict).
- `BaseTool._parse_input` returns dict input unchanged; `_to_args_and_kwargs`
  passes all keys as kwargs.
- `StructuredTool._arun` forwards kwargs to the stored coroutine.

If the test does not pass as written, tell me and I will fix it rather than
leave it for a maintainer.

issue.title: Markdown writers: escape thematic break and setext lookalikes
issue.body:
Closes #11992, closes #11993, closes #11994.

Three separate round-trip bugs in the Markdown writers. They touch
overlapping code (`Markdown/Inline.hs`, `Markdown.hs`), so they are in one
PR; I can split them if you prefer.

**#11992 — lines that read back as thematic breaks or setext headings.**
A paragraph, or a line after a `LineBreak`, consisting only of dashes or
equals was written unescaped and read back as a thematic break or setext
heading underline. `escapeLineStart` now escapes the first character of
such a run, but only when `escapeText` leaves the run untouched, so
`markdown` with `smart` keeps its existing `\-\--` and gains nothing new.
The wrapping case is handled separately: `avoidBadWraps` keeps a final run
of dashes or equals on the previous line instead of adding a backslash to
ordinary text, which is what #3542 was worried about.

**#11993 — adjacent `Code` inlines.**
Two adjacent code spans were written back to back, so the closing backtick
of the first and the opening backtick of the second formed a run of two
inside one span; the result read back as a single `Code` containing
backticks. Markdown cannot express two adjacent code spans, so adjacent
`Code` inlines are now merged into one span with the combined text — but
only when nothing would be written between them. When the first span has
attributes that the writer emits, the spans are already separated by the
`{...}` and no merge happens.

**#11994 — link titles and character references in destinations.**
Titles were written between double quotes without escaping `"` or `\`,
which made gfm and commonmark readers fail to recognize the link at all;
images and reference-link definitions used the same code. Destinations
were written as is, so `¶` in a URL was decoded to `¶` on read back.
Titles are now escaped, and `&` is escaped when it begins a character
reference, mirroring what `escapeText` already does for text.

`test/writer.markdown` gains the escaped titles on three lines; all three
tests are in `test/command`.

comment.body:
You are right that the writer's output is identical either way. The
difference shows on reading it back — the destination silently changes:

```
$ printf '%s' '[Para [Link ("",[],[]) [Str "x"] ("https://example.test/?q=one¶=two","")]]' \
  | pandoc -f native -t gfm | pandoc -f gfm -t native
[ Para
    [ Link
        ( "" , [] , [] )
        [ Str "x" ]
        ( "https://example.test/?q=one\182=two" , "" )
    ]
]
```

`¶` becomes `¶` (U+00B6), so the URL a reader gets is not the URL
that was written. With the `&` escaped the round trip is exact.

That is also why the old test could not catch it: it compared writer
output only. I have replaced it with a pipe test
(`pandoc -f native -t gfm | pandoc -f gfm -t native`) that asserts the
destination survives.

Separately, CI found a real miss of mine: `test/writer.opml` also carries
these titles (the OPML writer renders notes as Markdown), and I had only
updated `test/writer.markdown`. Both goldens are updated now.

issue.body:
Closes #12001.

This is the part of #11888 that c8c68ec0a did not reach. With
`rebase_relative_paths` and several input files, a relative path in a
footnote definition or a grid table that ends a file was rebased against

re-parsed from a string starting at the table's own position.

heading, and covers both an end-of-file footnote definition and an

issue.title: Table: VoiceOver reads the cell position instead of the column header

labels.name: user-5fafaa50/repo-7839c985
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

issue.body:
### What happened?

When moving between body cells, VoiceOver reads the cell's position, so it is hard to tell which column a value belongs to.

### Steps

Flags: `table.refresh` and `table.refreshNewFeatures` on. Gdev dashboard "Panel Tests - Table - Kitchen Sink", panel 1.

1. Turn on VoiceOver.
2. Move into the table body and use the arrow keys to go from cell to cell.

### Expected

VoiceOver reads the column header with each cell.

### Actual

VoiceOver reads the cell's position, for example "3 of 5", and not the column name.

Found in a manual VoiceOver pass. No e2e test yet. This may be a limitation of how the grid role is announced; a triage by someone who owns table accessibility would help.

Found during the Table 13.4 bug bash, part of grafana/grafana-org#1000. Case 16.4.

comment.body:
Triaging the root cause while looking at this area (I've submitted PRs for #135901 and #135904):

**Root cause is in `@grafana/react-data-grid`, not in Grafana's Table wrapper.**

The grid renders body cells with `role="gridcell"` and `aria-colindex`, but never associates them with their column header via `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby`. The header cells (`role="columnheader"`) also have no `id` that cells could reference. Without that association, VoiceOver falls back to announcing the cell's position within the row.

**Two possible fix paths:**

1. **In `@grafana/react-data-grid`** (the correct place): give each header cell a stable `id` (e.g. `{gridId}-header-{colIdx}`), then set `aria-describedby` on each `gridcell` pointing to that id. This is the standard ARIA grid pattern and would fix the announcement for all react-data-grid consumers, not just Grafana's Table.

2. **In Grafana's `render-hooks.tsx`** (workaround): add `aria-label={`${column.key}: ${formattedValue}`}` to each cell wrapper in `renderCellRoot`. This works but adds a per-cell string computation cost and isn't the canonical ARIA association pattern.

I'd recommend path 1 — a follow-up in `@grafana/react-data-grid` to emit header-cell IDs and cell-to-header references would fix this properly and make the Grafana-level workaround unnecessary. Happy to help with that PR if the maintainers agree on the approach.

issue.title: 音效磁贴缺少播放状态与收藏状态的无障碍标注
issue.body:
**现象**：白噪音磁贴（button）仅靠文字/颜色表达播放状态，无 `aria-pressed`；收藏星标是 `span[role=button]` 但无 `aria-label`（只有 title，且未选中时 opacity-0 对读屏器不可见）。

**期望**：
1. 音效磁贴加 `aria-pressed={sound.isPlaying}`；
2. 星标加 `aria-label={已收藏?取消收藏:收藏} + 音效名`；
3. 分类/只看收藏过滤按钮加 `aria-pressed`。

**验收**：读屏器遍历音效面板时能正确播报每个磁贴的开/关与收藏状态。

issue.title: 设置弹窗不支持 Esc 键关闭
issue.body:
**现象**：底栏各浮层（声音抽屉/视觉氛围/睡眠菜单）已支持 Esc 关闭，但设置弹窗（Settings Modal）没有监听 Esc——只能点击遮罩或右上角 ✕。

**期望**：`isOpen` 时监听 keydown Escape → 调用 `onClose()`；同时注意 Esc 不应同时触发 FocusView 的清屏退出逻辑（需 stopPropagation 或判断弹层状态）。

**验收**：设置弹窗打开时按 Esc 关闭，且不会顺带触发其他快捷键行为。

issue.title: TopNav「纯音乐」按钮跳转外部 YouTube，与内置自习电台脱节
issue.body:
**现象**：顶栏「纯音乐」按钮执行 `window.open('https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=lofi+study+music+live')` 跳转外部 YouTube 搜索页。但应用现在已内置完整的「自习电台」（4 个 24/7 电台流 + 网易云歌单 + 外链播放），该按钮与现有能力重复且把用户带离应用。

**期望**：改为打开声音工作台抽屉并自动定位到「🎵 自习电台」Tab（需要把 BottomBar 的抽屉开合状态提升或暴露打开请求）。

**验收**：点击「纯音乐」→ 抽屉滑出且选中自习电台 Tab，不再跳转外部。

issue.title: 「声音工作台」电台简介文案硬编码中文，缺 i18n
issue.body:
**现象**：声音工作台 → 自习电台 → 电台简介描述（如「经典柔和低保真节拍 · 慢节奏专注」「雨夜都市爵士萨克斯 · 惬意咖啡厅」等 4 条）以及若干子页小标题为硬编码中文，切换 English 后中英混排。

**位置**：`components/SoundMixer.tsx` 中 `STUDY_RADIOS` 常量的 `desc` 字段；另有「24/7 免版权自习电台」等区块小标题。

**期望**：desc 改为 `descKey` 引用 i18n（zh/en 双语），区块小标题同样收口。

**验收**：切换 English 后电台列表无中文残留。
